title: Dispatch from the Future: building an AI-native Company – Dan Shipper, Every, AI & I
talk_summary: Dan Shipper describes Every's 'compounding engineering' loop (plan, delegate, assess, codify) where lessons from each agent task are written back into prompts/CLAUDE.md/subagents so each feature makes the next easier. He reports 99% AI-written code, four products run by 15 people with single-developer ownership, and second-order effects like cross-repo code sharing and day-one new-hire productivity.

takeaways.technique: Codify step: write lessons back into agent config
takeaways.what_they_do: After each plan/delegate/assess cycle, they convert tacit knowledge (bugs found, plan fixes, review feedback) into explicit prompts in CLAUDE.md, subagents, and slash commands, building a shared library.

takeaways.technique: Agent code review as one assess layer, not sole gate
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat assessment as a stack: tests, manual trial, agent self-check, human code review, and agent code review, rather than a single gate.

takeaways.technique: Cross-repo agent reading for tacit code sharing
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of abstracting shared code into libraries, they point an agent at a neighboring repo to learn the process and re-implement it in the target stack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can just point your cloud code instance at um the repo from the developer sitting next to you and learn the process

takeaways.technique: Fractured-attention delegation to fill idle agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Work is dispatched as 'investigate this bug' tasks that run async while the human/agent does something else, then returns a plan or root-cause fix.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can kind of like get a meeting and say, "Hey, like I want you to investigate this bug." And then go do something else

takeaways.technique: Demo culture over memos for risky ideas
takeaways.what_they_do: Because prototyping is cheap, they build a quick demo instead of writing a memo/deck, letting people 'feel' weird ideas before committing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can vibe code something in a couple hours that sort of shows the thing that you're that you want to make

takeaways.technique: Single-owner per product with cross-product PRs
takeaways.what_they_do: Each app has one owning developer; anyone who hits a paper cut can have an agent fix it and submit a PR to that owner.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they will often just uh just submit a pull request for it to the other GM of the app
